Rashi on Meilah 2a:10:1.hebrew: דקבלה בדרום היא - דהיא עיקר עבודה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:10:1.english: That the collection is in the south - For it is the main service.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:11:1.english: Because [it is] daytime, it is the time of sacrifice.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:11:2.hebrew: ה"ג - אבל שחט בלילה וזרק ביום, ובלילה לאו זמן הקרבה הוא, והאי דשחט בלילה, אימא וכו':
Rashi on Meilah 2a:11:2.english: This is the text - "But if one slaughtered at night and sprinkled during the day, and night is not a time of sacrifice, and this [case] where one slaughtered at night, I would say [that it is removed from misuse]" etc.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:12:1.hebrew: ואי תנא שחטה בלילה וכו' אבל שחט ביום וזרק בלילה - וה"ה אם שחט בלילה וזרק בלילה, דזריקה דעיקר עבודה היא, הויא בלילה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:12:1.english: And if it taught 'he slaughtered it at night,' etc. 'But if he slaughtered during the day and sprinkled at night' - And the same applies if he slaughtered at night and sprinkled at night, since the sprinkling, which is the main service, took place at night.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:12:2.hebrew: אימא כמאן דחנקינון דמי קא משמע לן - דמועלין בזריקה דלילה, לאו מחוסר זמן הוא. והאי בעל הש"ס דייק ממתניתין, ולא ס"ל דזו ואצ"ל זו קתני:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:12:2.english: I would say, it is as if they were strangled; [the mishna] teaches us - that one is liable for misuse [of sacrifices whose blood is sprinkled] at night, for it is not [a case of] lacking the [proper] time. And this author of the Talmud infers [this] from the mishna, and does not hold that [the mishna] teaches "this, and it goes without saying [that]" the other.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:13:1.hebrew: חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו למאי חזו - כלומר, כל הני דתני במתניתין בדין הוא דמועלין בהן: דהאי דשחטן בדרום ראוי לקדשים קלים, כדאמרינן לעיל. ושחט בלילה נמי, או זרק בלילה, דין הוא דמועלין בהן, דלילה לאו מחוסר זמן הוא. אלא שחט על מנת להקטיר חוץ לזמנו או חוץ למקומו, למאי חזיא הא שחיטה דמועלין בה? הא פגול הוי, ולא חזו לא אימורין [לגבוה] ולא בשר לכהנים, ולא הוו קדשים ראויין כלל, ואמאי מועלין בהן:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:13:1.english: Beyond its time or beyond its place — for what are they fit? - That is to say: All these cases that are taught in the mishna, it is logical that one is liable for misuse with them. For [in the case of] one who slaughtered them in the south, [the animal] is fit for offerings of lesser sanctity, as we said above. And [in the case of] one who slaughtered at night, or who sprinkled at night, it is also logical that one is liable for misuse with them, since night is not [a case of] lacking the [proper] time. But [in the case of] one who slaughtered with the intent to burn [the offering] beyond its time or beyond its place — for what is it fit, this slaughtering for which one is liable for misuse? It is piggul, and neither the sacrificial parts [for the Most High] nor the meat for the priests are fit, and they are not consecrated items that are fit at all. So why is one liable for misuse with them?

Rashi on Meilah 2a:14:1.hebrew: ומשני הואיל ומרצין לפיגולן - כלומר: הואיל והאי שחיטת פיגול חשיבא כולי האי, דלעולם לא מיקבע בפיגול לחייבו כרת עד שיקרבו כל מתירין, שיזרק הדם, כדאמרינן במס' זבחים (דף כח:): "פגול הוא לא ירצה", ואמרינן: כהרצאת כשר, דכתיב ביה "ירצה לכפר", כך הרצאת פסול דפיגול. מה הרצאת כשר לא הורצה עד שיקרבו כל מתיריו לשמו, כך הרצאת פסול לא נקבע פסול פיגול לחייבו כרת עד שיקרבו כל מתיריו לשם פיגול. והיינו "מרצין", שמרצה (לצורך) הזריקה למקבעיה בפיגול. וכיון דהא זריקה חשובה כל כך דצריכה מרצין לפיגול, אכתי לא יצאת מקדושתה, ומועלין בה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:14:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Since they render [it] accepted for their piggul - That is to say: Since this slaughter [done with the intention of] piggul is so significant, for [an offering] is never fixed as piggul, so as to render [the one who eats it] liable to karet, until all of its permitting factors have been offered, [namely] that the blood is sprinkled, as we say in tractate Zevaḥim (28b): "It is piggul; it shall not be accepted" (Leviticus 7:18). And we say: Like the acceptance of a valid [offering], regarding which it is written "it shall be accepted to atone for him" (Leviticus 1:4), so too is the acceptance of an invalid [offering] of piggul. Just as a valid offering is not accepted until all its permitting factors have been offered for its own sake, so too an invalid offering is not fixed as piggul, to render [one] liable to karet, until all its permitting factors have been offered for the sake of piggul. And this is [the meaning of] "render accepted," that the sprinkling renders [the offering] accepted so as to fix it as piggul. And since this sprinkling is so important that it requires "rendering accepted" for piggul, [the offering] has still not left its sanctity, and one is liable for misuse of it.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:1:1.hebrew: קדשי קדשים ששחטן בדרום - אע"ג דדינן לישחט בצפון, לא יצאו מקדושתן לגבי מעילה, שהנהנה מהן שוה פרוטה מעל. ומה שאומרת המשנה "כיצד שחטן" וכו', היינו דלא תימא שחטן בדרום וקיבל דמן בצפון — דהא הוי עיקר עבודה דמקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה, ומקבלה ואילך הוי בצפון — אלא אפילו שחטן בצפון וקיבל דמן בדרום, אף על גב דקבלה, דהיינו עיקר עבודה, היא בדרום שלא כדינן, אפילו הכי מועלין בהן:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:1:1.english: Offerings of the most sacred order that one slaughtered in the south - Even though their law is that they be slaughtered in the north, they did not leave their sanctity with regard to misuse, [so that] one who derives benefit from them worth a peruta has committed misuse. [The Mishnah's words] "How? If one slaughtered them," etc. [come] so that you should not say [that this applies only where] one slaughtered in the south and collected their blood in the north — since the main service is from the collection onward, which is a commandment of the priesthood, and from the collection onward it was in the north — but [to teach that] even if one slaughtered them in the north and collected their blood in the south, even though the collection, which is the main service, was in the south, contrary to their law, nevertheless one is liable for misuse of them.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:1.hebrew: וכן אם שחט ביום וזרק דמן בלילה - אע"ג דלילה לאו זמן הקרבה היא, מועלין בהן:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:1.english: And likewise, if he slaughtered by day and sprinkled their blood at night - Even though night is not a time for offering [sacrifices], one is liable for misuse of them.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:2.hebrew: וכן אם שחט בלילה וזרק ביום - והאי כל דכן הוא דמועלין בהן, דהא זריקה, דהיא עיקר עבודה, הוית ביום. וזו ואין צריך לומר זו קתני:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:2.english: And likewise, if he slaughtered at night and sprinkled during the day - And this [case] is all the more so one in which one is liable for misuse of them, for the sprinkling, which is the primary [Temple] service, took place during the day. And [the Mishnah] teaches "this, and it need not be said [that] this" [i.e., both cases, the second being the more obvious].

Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:3.hebrew: או ששחטן - בצפון ביום, וחישב עליהן לאוכלן חוץ לזמנן, דהיינו פיגול, ויש בו כרת:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:3.english: Or if he slaughtered them - In the north [of the Temple courtyard], during the day, and he intended with regard to them to eat them beyond their [designated] time, which is piggul, and it carries the penalty of karet.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:4.hebrew: או חוץ למקומן - דהיינו פיגול, ואין בו כרת, אפ"ה מועלין בהן. ותרוייהו, פיגול דחוץ לזמנו ופיגול דחוץ למקומו, מחד קרא נפקי (זבחים דף כח.) מ"ואם האכל יאכל מבשר זבח שלמיו" וגו', דאיתקש חוץ למקומו לחוץ לזמנו, וקרי ליה פיגול. אבל לא הוי פיגול גמור, דליחייב עליה כרת:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:2:4.english: Or outside its area - That is, [it is] piggul, and it carries no karet [excision]; nevertheless, one is liable for misuse of them. And both of them — piggul of beyond its time and piggul of beyond its area — derive from one verse (Zevachim 28a): "And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings be eaten" etc., for [the case of] beyond its area is compared to [the case of] beyond its time, and [the Torah] calls it piggul. But it is not a full piggul, such that one would be liable to karet for it.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:3:1.english: A principle Rabbi Yehoshua stated: any [animal] that had a period of permissibility to the priests - and afterward it was disqualified from them.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:3:2.hebrew: אין מועלין בה - דלא קרינא בה "מקדשי ה'" (ויקרא ה), הואיל וכבר היתה ראויה לכהנים:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:3:2.english: One does not misuse it - For we do not read concerning it "the holy things of the Lord" (Leviticus 5), since it was already fit for the priests.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:4:1.hebrew: ואיזו היא שהיתה לה שעת היתר לכהנים שלנה ושנטמאת - דהואיל ושחיטה וזריקה הוו כראוי, דהיתה ראויה לכהנים, אע"ג דשוב נפסלה בלינה או ביוצא, דהשתא לית בה היתר לכהנים — אין מועלין בה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:4:1.english: And which is that which had a period of permissibility for the priests — [one that] remained overnight, or that became impure - Since the slaughter and the sprinkling [of the blood] were done properly, as it was fit for the priests, even though it was subsequently disqualified through remaining overnight or through leaving [the Temple courtyard], so that now there is no permissibility of it for the priests — one is not liable for misuse of it.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:4:2.hebrew: שלנה - הבשר לאחר זריקה, או שנטמאת, או שיצאת חוץ לקלעים לאחר זריקה. דאף על גב דהשתא אינה ראויה לכהנים, הואיל והיתה לה שעת הכושר קודם שנפסלה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:4:2.english: [That] remained overnight - The meat, after the throwing [of the blood]; or [that] became impure, or [that] went out beyond the curtains [of the Temple courtyard] after the throwing [of the blood]. For even though now it is not fit for the priests, since it had a time of fitness before it was disqualified [there is no misuse].

Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:1.hebrew: ואי זו היא שלא היתה לה כו' שנשחטה חוץ לזמנה וכו' - וה"ה לכל הני דתנא ברישא — שחטה בדרום או בלילה — שלא היה להן שעת היתר לכהנים. והיינו טעמא דנקיט הני תרין, דחוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו, טפי מכל הני דתנא ברישא דמועלין בהן, דהני תרי איתקוש אהדדי, ומחד קרא נפקי במס' זבחים (דף כח.) מ"ואם האכל יאכל" וגו':
Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:1.english: "And which is that which did not have etc." "that was slaughtered beyond its time" etc. - And the same applies to all those that the Mishnah taught at the beginning — [if] one slaughtered it in the south [of the Temple courtyard] or at night — that they had no period of fitness for the priests. And this is the reason that [the Mishnah] mentioned these two, [namely] beyond its time and outside its place, more than all those it taught at the beginning with regard to which one is liable for misuse: because these two are juxtaposed to one another, and they are derived from one verse, in tractate Zevachim (28a), from "And if any of the flesh... be eaten" etc.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:2.hebrew: ושקבלו פסולין וזרקו את דמה - בטמאין מיירי, ובקרבנות יחיד, דלא הותרה בהן טומאה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:2.english: And that unfit [persons] collected and sprinkled its blood - It is speaking of impure [priests], and of individual offerings, regarding which impurity was not permitted.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:3.hebrew: ושקבלו פסולין - בעלי מומין. וה"ה נמי דתני ברישא להא:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:5:3.english: And [that] unfit [persons] collected - Those with blemishes. And the same applies [to other unfit persons]; it is that [the Mishnah] taught this one first.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:7:1.hebrew: ס"ד אמינא הואיל ואמר עולא - לקמן בפרק ולד חטאת (מעילה דף יב.): קדשים שמתו יצאו מידי מעילה דבר תורה, אבל מדרבנן אית בהו מעילה, כדאיתא לקמן:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:7:1.english: It entered my mind to say: Since Ulla said - Later, in the chapter [entitled] Veled Chatat (Meilah 12a): Consecrated animals that died are removed from [the law of] misuse by Torah law, but by rabbinic law they are [still] subject to misuse, as is stated later.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:7:2.hebrew: כמאן דחנקינון דמו - וליהוו כקדשים שמתו, דיצאו מידי מעילה, דלא חזו לא לגבוה ולא להדיוט, דאין פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים. קמ"ל דלא:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:7:2.english: As if they were strangled - And let them be like sacrificial animals that died, which have left the status of misuse, since they are fit neither for the Most High [i.e., the altar] nor for an ordinary person, as one may not redeem sacrificial animals in order to feed them to dogs. [The mishna] therefore teaches us that this is not so.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:8:1.hebrew: קדשים שמתו וכו' אבל ראוי הוא לקדשים קלים - כדתנן באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נה.): קדשים קלים שחיטתן בכ"מ בעזרה:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:8:1.english: "Sacrificial animals that died..." "But it is fit for offerings of lesser sanctity" - As we learned in [the chapter] "Eizehu Mekoman" (Zevachim 55a): Offerings of lesser sanctity may be slaughtered anywhere in the Temple courtyard.

Rashi on Meilah 2a:9:1.hebrew: למה לי למיתני כל הני - דתני במתניתין דמועלין בהן, ליתני חדא מינייהו, ואע"ג דלא נעשית כמצותו מועלין בו, וממילא ידענא דה"ה לכל הני:
Rashi on Meilah 2a:9:1.english: Why do I need [the mishna] to teach all of these? - That the mishna taught that one is liable for misuse with them, let it teach one of them, [from which we would learn] that even though it was not performed according to its commandment, one is liable for misuse with it; and automatically I would know that the same applies to all these others.

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:13:1.hebrew: חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו למאי חזו - כלומר, הוה ליה למימר דהוי כמאן דחנקינהו, דלא חזו למידי. וקשה, דמאי פריך השתא? והרי כל הני דתני במתניתין, כיון דאיכא מ"ד אם עלו לא ירדו, לא אמרינן כמאן דחנקינון; כל שכן דניחא טפי חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו, דלא נימא כמאן דחנקינהו, דהא לכולי עלמא אם עלו לא ירדו, כדפרישית לקמן. לכן נ"ל דגרסינן "חוץ למקומו למה לי?" כלומר: פשיטא דלא הוי כמאן דחנקינהו מטעמא דעלו לא ירדו, כדפרישית, דעדיף מכולהו. ומשני: הואיל ומרצה לפיגולו, כלומר, הא קמ"ל דזריקה לא מפקע מידי מעילה. דסד"א דאע"ג דפסולה, מ"מ מרצה לקבוע פיגול ולחייב כרת (ואע"ג) דבעינן בפיגול כהרצאת כשר, וא"כ תועיל נמי להוציאה מידי מעילה, קמ"ל. ונראה דוחק לפרש שלא היה יודע המקשה האמת שבא לומר דזריקה לא מפקע מידי מעילה, והא פי' לעיל דעל כרחיה הוא ממילתיה דר' יהושע. לכן נראה למורי הכי, דגרס שפיר "למאי חזו?" כלומר: ודאי ידענא דרבותא משום זריקה ע"כ, כדפרישית; מיהו מה חידוש יש, כיון שאין שום ראויות בזריקה, מהיכי תיתי דמפקע מידי מעילה? ומשני: הואיל ומרצה לפיגולו, ולהכי סלקא דעתך דזריקה מפקע מידי מעילה, קמ"ל דלא:
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:13:1.english: "Beyond its time and beyond its place — for what are they fit?" - That is, [the Gemara] should have said that it is like [the animals] were strangled, as they are not fit for anything. But this is difficult: What is [the Gemara] now asking? [After all,] all these [cases] taught in the Mishnah — since there is an opinion that "if they went up [on the altar] they do not come down," we do not say that it is like they were strangled; all the more so, it is easier [to say this] regarding beyond its time and beyond its place, that we should not say it is like they were strangled, for according to everyone, "if they went up they do not come down," as I explained below. Therefore it seems to me that the text reads: "Beyond its place — why do I need it?" That is: It is obvious that it is not like they were strangled, for the reason of "if they went up they do not come down," as I explained, which is the strongest of them all. And [the Gemara] answers: Since it effects acceptance for its piggul — that is, this it teaches us, that the throwing [of the blood] does not remove [the animal] from [the law of] misuse. For one might have thought that although it is invalid, nevertheless it effects acceptance to establish piggul and to render [one] liable to karet (even though we require for piggul [a rite] like the acceptance of a valid [offering]), and if so it should also avail to remove it from [the law of] misuse; therefore it teaches us. But it seems forced to explain that the questioner did not know the truth, [namely] that he came to say that throwing does not remove [an item] from [the law of] misuse, since it was already explained above that this is necessarily [derived] from the words of Rabbi Yehoshua. Therefore it seems to my teacher that the text reads properly "For what are they fit?" That is: I certainly know that the novelty is on account of the throwing, necessarily, as I explained; but what novelty is there, since there is nothing fit in the throwing, why would we think that it removes [the animal] from [the law of] misuse? And [the Gemara] answers: Since it effects acceptance for its piggul, and therefore one might have thought that throwing removes [it] from [the law of] misuse, it teaches us that it does not.

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:1.hebrew: קדשי קדשים - כגון חטאת ואשם ושלמי צבור, שיש בהן מעילה עד שיהא בהן שעת היתר לכהנים, דהיינו לאחר זריקה; דעד שעת זריקה מיקרו "קדשי ה'", ובאימורים אף לאחר זריקה. אבל בקדשים קלים אין בהן מעילה עד לאחר זריקה, שאז הוברר חלק גבוה, ואז יש מעילה באימוריהן:
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:1.english: Offerings of the most sacred order - For example, a sin offering, a guilt offering, and the communal peace offerings, in which there is misuse [of consecrated property] only once there is for them a time of permissibility for the priests, that is, after the sprinkling [of the blood]; for until the time of sprinkling they are called "sacred to the Lord," and with regard to the sacrificial portions [burned on the altar], even after the sprinkling. But with lesser sacred offerings, there is no misuse until after the sprinkling, for then the portion of the Most High has been clarified, and then there is misuse with regard to their sacrificial portions.

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:2.hebrew: ששחטן בדרום - ודינן לישחט בצפון, כדאי' בפ' איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מז.). מועלין בהן — בגמרא מפרש מאי רבותא. וא"ת: האי ששחטן בדרום, היכי דמי? אי דקבל בצפון — הא למה לי? תנינא בסמוך בסיפא. ואי דקבל בדרום — אם כן ברישא הוי ליה למיתני: ששחטו בדרום וקבל בצפון, וכן שחטו בצפון וקבל בדרום, דלא הוי רבותא כל כך כמו ששחטו בדרום וקבל בדרום! דסדר משנתינו כך הוא, ששונה אותו שיש בו חידוש יותר בסיפא, כדעביד בגמ' צריכותא. ולפי זה ששונה חידוש זה ברישא, א"כ תני "זו ואין צריך לומר זו", והדר תני "לא זו אף זו", ואין זו שיטת תנאים. דכולל ברישא שינוי מקום דדרום, והדר מפרש "כיצד" קתני, כלומר: כיצד הוי שינוי מקום דדרום שאמרו? כגון ששחטן בדרום וקבל בצפון כו'. אבל שחטן בדרום וקבל בדרום — בהא לא מיירי מתני'. ונראה לפום ריהטא דבכי ה"ג לית בהו מעילה, מדלא מפרש להו במתניתין, ויש טעם בדבר, משום דשינה בהו כ"כ. מיהו נראה למהר"ר פרץ שי' דאין זו סברא, דהא בגמ' מפרש טעמא דמתניתין דמועלין בהן אע"ג דשינה ועשה בפסול, משום דהוא ראוי לקדשים קלים, וא"כ מה לי חד פסול מה לי תרי פסולי? לכן נ"ל דהוא הדין בשחט וקבל בדרום דמועלין. והא דלא תני במתניתין אע"ג דהוא רבותא טפי — כך דרך משנה, ולפי ששונה כל אחד בפני עצמו לא חש לשנותם ביחד, כדאשכחן בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נג:) דקתני "הבא על יבמתו בין בשוגג בין במזיד כו'", ובגמרא תני "אפילו שניהם", ובמשנה שייריה אע"ג דהוי רבותא טפי, משום דמסתמא כיון דשמעת חדא לריעותא ה"ה בתרתי:
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:2.english: That one slaughtered them in the south - Their law is that they must be slaughtered in the north, as stated in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 47a). "One is liable for misuse of them" — the Gemara explains what the novelty is. And if you ask: This case of one who slaughtered them in the south — what are its circumstances? If he [also] collected the blood in the north, why do I need this? We learn it shortly after, in the latter clause. And if he collected it in the south, then in the first clause [the Mishnah] should have taught: "that one slaughtered in the south and collected in the north, and likewise slaughtered in the north and collected in the south," for that is not as much of a novelty as [the case of] one who slaughtered in the south and collected in the south! [The answer is] that the order of our Mishnah is thus: it teaches the one containing the greater novelty in the latter clause, as the Gemara does in [its discussion of] the need for [each of the cases]. And according to this, if it taught this novelty in the first clause, then it should have taught "this, and needless to say that," and afterward taught "not only this, but even that" — and this is not the method of the Tannaim. Rather, it includes in the first clause the change of place of the south, and afterward explains, "How?" it teaches — that is: How is there a change of place of the south that they spoke of? For example, where one slaughtered them in the south and collected [the blood] in the north, etc. But [where one] slaughtered in the south and collected in the south, the Mishnah does not discuss this. And it appears at first glance that in such a case there is no misuse in them, since the Mishnah did not explain them, and there is a reason for the matter, because he changed so much in them. However, it appears to the Rabbi, Maharar Peretz, may he live, that this is not reasonable, for in the Gemara it explains the reason of the Mishnah — that one is liable for misuse of them even though he changed and acted in a disqualifying manner — because they are fit [to be treated as] lesser sacrifices; and if so, what difference does it make whether there is one disqualification or two disqualifications? Therefore it seems to me that the same applies where he slaughtered and collected in the south, that one is liable for misuse. And the fact that the Mishnah does not teach it, even though it is a greater novelty — such is the way of the Mishnah: since it teaches each one on its own, it did not bother to teach them together, as we find in the chapter [entitled] HaBa al Yevimto (Yevamot 53b), where it teaches, "One who has relations with his yevamah, whether unintentionally or intentionally," etc., and in the Gemara it teaches "even both," and in the Mishnah it omitted it even though it is a greater novelty, because presumably, since you heard one [case] as a disqualification, the same applies to two:

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:3.hebrew: שחטן בדרום וקבל דמן בצפון, שחטן בצפון וקבל דמן בדרום - בגמ' מפרש הטעם [הא] דתנן קבל בדרום: לרבותא, דאע"ג דשינה בקבלה דעיקר עבודה היא, מ"מ מועלין. שחט ביום וזרק בלילה, שחט בלילה וזרק ביום — כך הגירסא ברוב הספרים, ונראה לר"י שהוא שיבוש, דאית ליה למיתני אותו שהוא חידוש יותר בסיפא, כמו גבי דרום. אלא גרסינן איפכא: שחט בלילה וזרק ביום, שחט ביום וזרק בלילה, דזריקה עיקר עבודה, והויא חידוש יותר כששינה בזריקה דאיכא מעילה. ולהכי שביק קבלה גבי לילה ונקט זריקה, משום דאי אפשר לצמצם שתהא שחיטה ממש בסוף הלילה והקבלה מיד ביום, דקבלה ושחיטה תכופות זו לזו:
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:1:3.english: If one slaughtered them in the south and collected their blood in the north, [or] slaughtered them in the north and collected their blood in the south - In the Gemara it explains [the reason] that the Mishnah taught "collected in the south": to emphasize that even though he altered the collection, which is the main service, nevertheless one is liable for misuse. "He slaughtered by day and threw [the blood] at night; he slaughtered at night and threw by day" — so is the reading in most books, but it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that this is an error, for [the Tanna] should have taught the case that is a greater novelty in the latter clause, as with the case of the south. Rather, we read it in reverse: "he slaughtered at night and threw by day; he slaughtered by day and threw at night," since the throwing is the main service, and it is a greater novelty when he altered the throwing, in that there is [still] misuse. And therefore [the Tanna] omitted collection with regard to night and mentioned throwing, because it is impossible to calibrate so that the slaughter would be exactly at the end of the night and the collection immediately in the day, since collection and slaughter follow immediately upon one another:

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:3:1.hebrew: כל שהיה לה שעת היתר לכהנים - שנעשית בזריקה, אין מועלין, דלא קרינא בהו "קדשי ה'":
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:3:1.english: Any [offering] that had a period of permissibility for the priests - [meaning, one] that was rendered [fit] through the sprinkling [of its blood], one does not commit me'ilah [with it], for we do not apply to them [the term] "holy things of the Lord."

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:6:1.hebrew: פשיטא משום דשחטן בדרום אפקינון מידי מעילה - וא"ת: לישני דהא קמ"ל דזריקה לא מהניא בהו לאפוקי מידי מעילה? י"ל: דהא פשיטא הוא, כיון שהזריקה בפסול דלא מהניא ולא מידי. ועוד י"ל דלפי מה שפירש מורי ניחא שפיר, ולקמיה אפרש בעזרת השם:
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:6:1.english: "Obvious! Because he slaughtered them in the south, have they been removed from [the law of] me'ilah?" - And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] answer that this is what [the Mishnah] teaches us — that sprinkling does not avail for them to remove them from [the law of] me'ilah? One can say: This is obvious, since the sprinkling was done in a disqualified [manner], it does not avail at all. And furthermore, one can say that according to what my teacher explained, it works out well, and below I will explain, with God's help:

Tosafot on Meilah 2a:7:1.hebrew: קדשים שמתו יצאו מידי מעילה כו' - דכיון שהולכין לאיבוד, לא איקרו "קדשי ה'":
Tosafot on Meilah 2a:7:1.english: "Sacrificial animals that died are excluded from [the laws of] misuse," etc. - For since they go to waste, they are not called "holy things of the Lord."
